source.title: Look But Don't Touch with Sparse Autoencoders for Unlearning in Diffusion Models
source.authors: E. Cassano; Riccardo Renzulli; Rayyan Ahmed; Marco Grangetto; S. Alaniz

page_placements.theme: Detection, decodability and recurrence do not establish selective control

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling, truncation, or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether SAE features used for direct concept intervention behave as controllable intervention points in diffusion models. It reports distribution shifts and visual artifacts from steering, and proposes detection-based replacement instead. This refines the claim about SAE features as representation units, but does not test superposition or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests SAE-based concept steering and reports activation-distribution shifts and artifact rates. Other reported results—including PER unlearning scores, padding ablations, adversarial robustness, and NSFW removal—primarily evaluate the proposed unlearning method rather than whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units, so they are not included as rows. Results cited from other work are also excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper uses existing SAEs (SAeUron, SAEmnesia, G-SAE, SDXL Turbo SAE) as tools for concept unlearning in diffusion models. Its own results are: (a) negative-multiplier steering pushes activations out of distribution and causes artifacts, and (b) its PER replacement method performs well. Neither result measures whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units (V5). Nor does any result measure superposition, capacity competition, polysemanticity causes or feature dimensionality (V1–V4, V6). The OOD shift reflects intervention magnitude (multipliers up to −30, or subtracting scaled decoder columns), so it is a steering-effect construct, not a property of the features as representational units. Concept detection and localization by SAE latents is shown only qualitatively, in diffusion models rather than LLMs. It is not reported as a test of sparse-feature recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE latents reliably detect and localize concepts, but multiplier-based steering yields OOD activations and artifacts. Detection should therefore be separated from intervention, e.g. via their patch embedding replacement (PER) method.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates SAE-based concept detection and intervention in diffusion models; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method or measure feature-overlap geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported distribution shift varies by SAE pipeline; the largest reported activation and norm deviations are for the SAE trained on SDXL Turbo. The text also states that larger multipliers make distribution shifts more extreme.

fits_no_version.finding: Negative-multiplier steering on SAE latents in SD v1.5 and SDXL Turbo puts 18.8–83.7% of activation values and 44.7–100% of norms outside the original distribution. VLM artifact rates are 43–61% versus a 1–2% baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intervening on SAE latents (dictionary features) as control knobs produces off-manifold activations and degraded outputs, even when those latents detect the concept well (detection–intervention gap).

record.problems: The evidence is limited to diffusion-model concept unlearning and does not test the superposition or capacity claims. Artifact rates use an automated VLM evaluator; the reported activation-distribution comparisons are summarized across patch-level activations, and uncertainty is not reported for those distribution figures.
record.rows_left_out: PER results and additional unlearning metrics were omitted because they primarily measure the proposed replacement method’s unlearning performance, not the direct-control-point claim. Cited findings from other work were not extracted.

untested.parts: All: toy-model superposition, geometry, sparsity transition.
All: no LLM measurements; diffusion-model concept localization is only qualitative (Fig. 7) and uses pre-trained SAEs.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features are not measured; only steering side effects are.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'challenges' label is removed. The paper does not address whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical; the OOD effect depends on large chosen multipliers. The paper is an unlearning-method paper (ECCV 2026) whose main contribution is PER. The artifact-rate judge is Qwen2-VL, partly validated by a human study (Krippendorff's α = 0.76).

relation.reason: Uses SAE representations as tools without testing superposition geometry, capacity-driven polysemanticity, dictionary completeness, stability or canonicality, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: Uses SAE concept detection and decoder directions for diffusion-model unlearning; evaluates intervention distribution shifts, artifacts and PER performance. These results do not test V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The activation-value percentages use median negative multipliers; the statement rounds the minimum artifact rate from 43.1% to 43%. The source inconsistently describes SDXL Turbo's 83.7% as half; the recorded authors' conclusion otherwise matches the text.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SAE multiplier-based concept unlearning in the four reported diffusion-model pipelines
reader_labels.reason: Direct SAE steering produces substantial activation-distribution and norm shifts and elevated artifact rates relative to unmodified models, challenging the suitability of SAE features as reliable direct control points (R1–R12).
